title: Effect of atomisation pressure on particle size distribution and reconstitution behaviour of encapsulated ascorbic acid by spray drying

record.title: Effect of atomisation pressure on particle size distribution and reconstitution behaviour of encapsulated ascorbic acid by spray drying
record.abstract: Ascorbic acid solutions (20 % w/w) were spray-dried with maltodextrin DE 10–12 as wall material at wall-to-core ratios of 3:1, 4:1 and 5:1. Atomisation air pressure was varied between 1.5 and 3.5 bar in a two-fluid nozzle system. Outlet particle size (d50) ranged from 18 to 47 µm and was well described by a power-law correlation with atomisation pressure (R² = 0.93). Encapsulation efficiency, assessed by extracting surface versus total ascorbic acid, improved from 71 to 89 % as wall-to-core ratio increased. Reconstitution time in 50 mL of water at 25 °C was measured by turbidimetry and showed a 22 % reduction at higher atomisation pressure due to more porous particle structures revealed by SEM. Retention of ascorbic acid after 8 weeks at 38 °C and 75 % RH was above 85 % at the highest wall-to-core ratio tested.
